title: Perfect Forwarding Lab
hints: `Args&&` on a template parameter is a forwarding reference: it becomes `Tracer&` for an lvalue and `Tracer&&` for an rvalue. `std::forward<Args>(args)` passes each one on as what it was (lesson 11.01). Remove the `std::forward` once and watch the moves turn into copies.
requirements: A `Tracer` type that prints its copies and moves (the one from milestone 7 is fine)
`template <typename T, typename... Args> T makeObject(Args&&... args)` that forwards its arguments to `T`'s constructor
`emplaceInto(std::vector<T>& v, Args&&... args)` that forwards to `emplace_back`
Calls with an lvalue, an rvalue (`std::move` or a temporary) and a `const` object, with a comment for each saying how many copies and moves you expected and how many you saw
stretch: `invokeAndLog(f, args...)` that calls any function with forwarded arguments and returns its result with `decltype(auto)`.
